title: rapid-handoff-sketch-otto-lane
content:
Quick scratch for handing off Otto Lane to the onsite loop team

Context: took a ~45m paired coding + design session (remote collab) on 2025-11-02. This is raw — mostly verbs and quick impressions for whoever follows up. Use as input to panel and for pairing exercise tuning.

High-level vibe:
- Friendly, curious, low ego. Comfortable with asking clarifying Qs but occasionally over-indexed on edge-case correctness instead of moving forward.
- Good mental model of KV cache + batching tradeoffs (relevant to serving runtime). Uses analogies (cache as "hot lane") which helped communication.

Coding exercise (small lang model util):
- Prompt: implement a simplified token cache lookup + eviction hint function (pseudo-Python).
- Approach: wrote an iterative solution first, then refactored to a map-first O(1) lookup.
- Strengths: quickly identified hot-paths, added constant-time checks, avoided unnecessary list scans.
- Weakness: missed a subtle race on concurrent writes (I called it out); candidate acknowledged but didn't propose a full locking strategy — suggested optimistic write + compare-and-swap but no concrete API sketch.
- Outcome: working prototype, added 3 quick unit-test ideas.

System-design mini (10–15m):
- Prompt: design a per-tenant cache invalidation signal for a large multitenant inference fleet.
- Candidate sketched pub/sub invalidation + versioned keys. Suggested storing invalidation tokens in a small in-memory store and using KV TTL for soft-expiry.
- Liked: concrete tradeoffs — push vs pull, network overhead vs freshness.
- Needs work: didn't discuss how to shard tokens under heavy churn, or how to handle cross-region consistency.

Communication & collaboration:
- Good at explaining thought process, will verbalize tradeoffs and ask for constraints.
- When pressed on timelines, tends to dive into correctness weeds instead of saying "MVP then iterate" — coaching note for interviewers to ask timeboxing followups.

Ownership & product sense:
- Gave a short anecdote about shipping a perf optimization on an inference pipeline at last job: described A/B metrics, rollback plan, and stakeholder comms. That felt credible and product-oriented.

Red flags / risk areas:
- Concurrency thinking is moderate — understands concepts but needs prompting to convert to concrete designs (mutex vs atomics vs sharding).
- Not convinced on operational debugging patterns under noisy production loads (didn't mention tracing/span annotations or example metrics to triage).

Suggested interview focus areas for the panel:
- One focused concurrency prompt: design a safe concurrent cache update path (ask for APIs, failure modes, and benchmark signals).
- Operational troubleshooting scenario: given a 2x p50 latency regression in region A, what logs/metrics/traces do you pull and what immediate mitigations do you perform?
- Pairing exercise with reviewer on a small PR: watch for willingness to accept suggestions and iterate quickly.

Suggested scorecard (quick, numeric):
- Coding correctness & speed: 3/5
- Systems design (small scale): 4/5
- Concurrency & correctness at scale: 3/5
- Communication & team fit: 4/5
- Ownership & product judgment: 4/5
- Overall bar (recommendation): consider-for-full-loop (lean hire after strong concurrency + ops probe)

Unresolved questions to surface to panel:
- Where did they actually ship the cache optimization? repo link? can we see the PR mentioned in anecdote? (linked_artifacts includes a guess PR above; confirm).
- Can they describe a concrete incident where they used tracing/spans to find a root cause?
- What is their most comfortable language for low-latency runtime work (they said Go/Python; ask for examples in Go).

Action items (for handoff):
- Ask Diego to run 15m concurrency follow-up on next panel (concurrent cache write).
- Maya to own ops troubleshooting probe in onsite loop.
- I (Kai) will ping recruiting to check reference that mentions the PR.

Notes-to-self (meta):
- Keep this as a lightweight guide — candidate is promotable for eng team, but need to validate scale/concurrency instincts before final.
- For interviewers: avoid coding tasks that reward over-engineering; timebox the exercise and call out "build an MVP in 15m then iterate."

End of scratchpad.
recommended_next_steps: schedule 30m concurrency probe (Diego) + 20m ops troubleshooting (Maya); follow up on PR link and reference check. If passes, invite to full loop with one more systems interview focused on sharding/consistency.
